body:
This might be macOS dynamically syncing frames based on the display or input events.

**Try this:**

1. Go to System Settings > Displays
2. Select your 75Hz monitor
3. Manually set the refresh rate to 75Hz again, even if it already shows that
4. Restart your system.

you can also try launching the project with the `--single-window` flag if you’re using multi-window mode, or just open the project on the 120Hz display as a workaround.

_bubu07codes_

The behavior still occurs after trying those steps, whether using multi-window or single-window mode.

It does of course work to just run the project on the 120Hz display, though this is rather inconvenient in my case and ideally shouldn't be necessary 😄

After additional testing, it seems switching to different refresh rates yields similar behavior:

The frame rate always caps at double the display's refresh rate (120fps @ 60Hz, 100fps @ 50Hz).

Also, the problem still occurs even after setting both displays to 60Hz and restarting.

I would be curious if this is reproducible by others on macOS with dual monitors.

I can confirm this on macOS 15.5 (M4 Max MacBook Pro built-in 120 Hz display), on both Metal and MoltenVK. Once the cursor enlarges during fast motion (macOS feature), it's locked to the monitor refresh rate (120 FPS). Before the cursor enlarges, it will run at a significantly lower FPS (highly variable 250-350 FPS) than when the cursor isn't moving (700 FPS). The cursor will also look jittery before it enlarges, but not once it enlarges. I've tried disabling HDR on the display profile just in case it affected something, but it didn't change the results.

Compatibility is not affected at all: FPS remains very high throughout, regardless of mouse motion or whether the cursor is enlarged.

Simillar issue on v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] and MacOS Tahoe 26.2 (25C56) and MacBook M4 Max 16 / 36.

However, for me it doesn't even depend on mouse movement, sometimes project just capped at monitor's refresh rate even with disabled vsync. It's super tricky to reproduce because it's also for some reasond depends on embeding the game to the editor.

For example:

1. Created empty project, disable vsync and run (default window size) ~around 1800-2500 FPS.
2. Embed game window to the editor + make it floating ~around 4500 FPS.
3. Turn off embedding: ~1200 FPS.

And at the same time the different empty project just capped ~300-400 FPS all the time, no matter if vsync is enabled or disabled and neverthless of embedding, window size, etc.

I understand, that fluctuating high fps values are totally fine, but capped framerate with disabled vsync is something strange, since machine is definitely capable to render game at higher rr.

Also, i have two external monitors, one of them with HDR, tried to turn it off, change refresh rate on both monitors, but it seems like have no effect. Honestly, don't know where to dig at this point.



UPD: Figured out, that this is only reproducible when using metal rendering backend. In compatibility mode using opengl empty project skyrockets up to 8000 fps on my chip. This issue is probably related: [114258](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/114258)

UPD2: Reproducible not only using metal backend, but vulkan as well. Basically, only Compatibility mode doesn't seems to have an issue, both Mobile and Forward+ with any of backends (metal, vulkan) capped to monitor's RR.

Possibly an additional, deterministic way to reproduce the refresh-rate cap on macOS 26: with `VSYNC_DISABLED` and `Engine.max_fps = 0`, the frame rate is uncapped only while the window's content area is off screen. As soon as any part of the content is on screen (the whole window, or a 100 px strip), drawn frames lock to the display refresh (60 Hz here). Moving the content off screen again unlocks it. No mouse movement is involved. Compatibility/OpenGL3 is not affected.

**Environment**

- Godot 4.7.1.stable and 4.7.2.stable (official builds), same result on both.
- macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), MacBook Air with Apple M4 (`Apple M4 (Apple9)`).
- Two displays: built-in 2880×1864 scaled to 1710×1041 pt (the window runs there, 60 Hz) and an external 2560×1440 @ 60 Hz.
- Empty project (default `project.godot`, only `config/name` set), the script below started with `--script`, no editor involved, window 640×400.

**Result** (drawn frames per second over 2.5 s steps; `Engine.get_frames_drawn()` deltas, equal to main-loop iterations in every step; `window_can_draw()` true; `window_get_vsync_mode()` reports `DISABLED` throughout)

| Step | 4.7.2 Mobile/Metal | 4.7.2 Forward+/Metal | 4.7.1 Mobile/Metal | 4.7.2 Compatibility/OpenGL3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1. content off screen | 1363 | 2121 | 1810 | 2056 |
| 2. window fully on screen | 60.5 | 63.4 | 64.8 | 2112 |
| 3. off screen again | 843 | 394 | 583 | 2095 |
| 4. 100 px strip of content on screen | 60.0 | 60.0 | 71.2 | 2069 |
| 5. off screen again | 823 | 611 | 462 | 2159 |

(4.7.1 Forward+/Metal behaves like 4.7.2. "Off screen" = the window positioned so that its content is below the bottom edge of the display; macOS keeps the title bar reachable, so only the title bar stays visible. The first column is a plain launch with no overrides; the other three were launched with `display/window/size/always_on_top=true` and `no_focus=true` in an `override.cfg` so the window would not take focus — the pattern is the same either way.)

In a separate script (4.7.1, Mobile/Metal) none of the following removed the cap while the content stayed on screen: setting `VSYNC_DISABLED` again, `ENABLED → DISABLED`, `MAILBOX → DISABLED`, moving the window, minimizing and restoring, toggling `WINDOW_FLAG_ALWAYS_ON_TOP`, resizing between 1280×800 and the full display size.

For what it is worth, `SurfaceLayer::resize()` in `drivers/metal/rendering_context_driver_metal.cpp` calls `setDisplaySyncEnabled(false)` for `VSYNC_DISABLED` on every swap-chain rebuild and `present()` uses plain `presentDrawable`, so the engine-side state looks right; the pacing only appears once the layer is actually composited on a display.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Empty project; save the script below as `vsync_probe.gd` next to `project.godot`.
2. `Godot --path . --rendering-method mobile --rendering-driver metal --script vsync_probe.gd` — steps 2 and 4 print ~60 drawn/s, steps 1, 3, 5 print hundreds or thousands.
3. `Godot --path . --rendering-method gl_compatibility --rendering-driver opengl3 --script vsync_probe.gd` — thousands in every step.

```gdscript
extends SceneTree
# VSYNC_DISABLED with Engine.max_fps = 0: frame rate versus the window's
# position on screen. Counts both main-loop iterations and drawn frames.

const STEP_SECONDS := 2.5

var _phase := 0.0
var _spinner: ColorRect


func _initialize() -> void:
	call_deferred("_run")


func _run() -> void:
	await _frames(5)
	var rect := ColorRect.new()
	rect.color = Color(0.2, 0.3, 0.4)
	rect.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	root.add_child(rect)
	_spinner = ColorRect.new()
	_spinner.color = Color(0.9, 0.8, 0.2)
	_spinner.size = Vector2(60, 60)
	root.add_child(_spinner)

	var screen := DisplayServer.window_get_current_screen()
	var screen_rect := Rect2i(DisplayServer.screen_get_position(screen), DisplayServer.screen_get_size(screen))
	var usable := DisplayServer.screen_get_usable_rect(screen)
	# Content below the bottom edge of the display; macOS keeps the title bar reachable.
	var off_screen := Vector2i(screen_rect.end.x - 80, screen_rect.end.y)
	var on_screen := usable.position + Vector2i(40, 60)
	var strip := Vector2i(usable.end.x - 100, usable.position.y + 60)

	root.size = Vector2i(640, 400)
	root.position = off_screen
	await _frames(10)
	Engine.max_fps = 0
	DisplayServer.window_set_vsync_mode(DisplayServer.VSYNC_DISABLED)
	print("VSYNC_PROBE godot=%s os=%s %s method=%s driver=%s gpu=%s screen=%s usable=%s refresh=%.1f" % [
		Engine.get_version_info().string, OS.get_name(), OS.get_version(),
		RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_method(), RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_driver_name(),
		RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_name(), screen_rect, usable, DisplayServer.screen_get_refresh_rate(screen)])

	await _measure("1_off_screen")
	root.position = on_screen
	await _measure("2_fully_on_screen")
	root.position = off_screen
	await _measure("3_off_screen")
	root.position = strip
	await _measure("4_strip_100px_on_screen")
	root.position = off_screen
	await _measure("5_off_screen")
	quit(0)


func _measure(name: String) -> void:
	await _frames(10)
	var iterations := 0
	var drawn_start := Engine.get_frames_drawn()
	var started := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	while (Time.get_ticks_usec() - started) / 1_000_000.0 < STEP_SECONDS:
		await process_frame
		iterations += 1
		_phase += 0.05
		_spinner.position = Vector2(100 + 60 * cos(_phase), 100 + 60 * sin(_phase))
	var elapsed := (Time.get_ticks_usec() - started) / 1_000_000.0
	var drawn := Engine.get_frames_drawn() - drawn_start
	print("VSYNC_PROBE %s iterations/s=%.1f drawn/s=%.1f engine_fps=%.1f vsync=%d max_fps=%d can_draw=%s position=%s size=%s" % [
		name, iterations / elapsed, drawn / elapsed, Engine.get_frames_per_second(),
		DisplayServer.window_get_vsync_mode(), Engine.max_fps, DisplayServer.window_can_draw(),
		DisplayServer.window_get_position(), DisplayServer.window_get_size()])


func _frames(count: int) -> void:
	for _i in count:
		await process_frame
```
